adam.headline: Wins the turnover trade and the matchups, then freezes on contested catches.
text: Adam gives the ball away 1.4 times a game against a league middle of 2.2, and he has forced 16 turnovers against 8 giveaways, the best trade in the league. His set-ups are worth 0.80 points a shot, third best, and 36% of them go in.
On defense he is beaten on 11% of shots (middle 20%), opponents shoot 19% when he stays in front (middle 30%), and he carries 1.30x an even share of the defending. Reilly made 2 of 12 against him.

The habit to fix: when a pass reaches him with a defender close, he holds the ball first, 9 times in 12. Shooting on the catch or moving it straight on would help a shooter who sits right at the league middle for TS (37%).

zach.headline: Shoots the most, gets open a lot, and needs the next one to go in.
text: Zach has taken 41 shots in 6 games, 68% of them open, and made them at 31% TS against a league middle of 37%. The looks are average for where he shoots (+0.02 a shot), so this is finishing, not shot selection. He is also the most improved player of the season, up 3.8 two-way a game from his early nights to his late ones.

The pressure is real: 22 forced turnovers, the most in the league, against 19 giveaways. Viraj got beaten on 5 of 12 shots guarding him, but when Viraj stayed in front, Zach went 0 for 7. Opponents shoot 39% over Zach when he stays in front (middle 30%).

Rebounding is the quiet cost: 1.6 a game, and only 1.0 once uncontested ones count half, the lowest of anyone. Across 54 results his teams win 13.7 points of win chance less than expected (17-37), the clearest signal in the league. More boards are the way out.

alex.headline: Wins the boards and hands the ball back.
text: Alex is the best rebounder among players with five or more games: 3.6 a game, and 2.3 once uncontested ones count half (middle 1.9).

The shots come from hard spots: 0.13 points a shot below the league, at 29% TS. When a pass reaches him in a contest he holds the ball every time (5 of 5), and the looks he sets up for others are worth 0.34 points a shot, among the lowest in the league (middle 0.63).
He gives the ball away 3.2 times a game, second only to Reilly, and that is the biggest swing available to him. He is beaten on a third of shots (5 of 15), but he held Ian to 0 for 10.

ben.headline: Nobody gets past him, and teammates keep wasting his passes.
text: Ben has never been tagged as beaten, 0 of 12 shots. Opponents shoot 17% when he is in position, and Adam, one of the better scorers, is 5 of 14 against him. He leads both the MVP race (43.6) and the Defender race (29.6).

He scores at 49% TS, well above the league middle of 37%, while taking harder looks than most (only 45% of his shots are open), and he gives the ball away 1.0 times a game, the fewest in the league. He forces only 6 turnovers, so he is a wall more than a ball hawk.

He sets up 6.0 shots a game, level with Evan for the most, but only 26% go in, and teammates held the ball first on 13 of his 19 contested set-ups. That part is on the receivers. Over 55 results his teams win 7.8 points of win chance more than expected (33-22).

g-ian.headline: Stays in front of everyone and leaves the shooting to others.
text: Ian is beaten on 9% of shots (1 of 11) and held Alex to 4 of 20, the busiest matchup on film. When opponents do shoot over him, though, they hit 40%.

His set-ups are good looks, 0.82 points a shot with 37% going in, second only to Reilly, and teammates held the ball first on 7 of his 11 contested ones. He and Adam are 4-2 together, the best pair in the league.
He has taken 15 shots in 4 games at 27% TS, so scoring is not his job yet. His rebounds are hard-won, 71% of them contested. His win impact is about zero (9-7).

evan.headline: Three games, three wins, and the best looks of anyone with real volume.
text: Evan scores at 58% TS on shots worth 0.38 points more than the league average, the best of anyone with more than 10 shots, and only 37% of his shots are open. He gives it away 1.3 times a game and forced 11 turnovers against 4 giveaways.

He passes a lot, 6.0 set-ups a game, but into tough spots worth 0.51 points a shot. Most of his assists came from teammates holding and then making a contested shot, so his Real AST is 0.6 against 1.6 assists.

He carries a light defensive load (0.67x an even share) and was beaten on 2 of 6 shots. His +29 on Win chance added is the most in the league, and he is 12-4 over every result. Three filmed games is still an early read.

g-lukas.headline: Seven shots, great looks, and teams that keep winning.
text: Lukas has 71% TS on the best shot quality in the league (+0.42), but on 7 shots in 3 games.

He plays off the ball, with almost no set-ups (0.4 a game), and is rarely the tagged defender (0.39x an even share). When he is, the shots have gone in (beaten on 2 of 5), on far too few to judge. He rebounds more than anyone, 3.9 a game, 2.8 once uncontested ones count half.
His teams are 11-3 over every result, +9.2 points of win chance from having him. Three filmed games is still an early read.

reilly.headline: Draws the hardest assignments and makes the best passes.
text: Reilly carries the heaviest defensive load in the league, 1.40x an even share. He is rarely beaten (13%), but opponents still hit 43% over him, which is what guarding the best scorers looks like. Adam is 1 of 8 against him when he stays in front.
His set-ups are worth 1.08 points a shot and 55% of them go in, the best passing by quality on film, and he leads the league with 2.3 assists a game.

The ball is the problem: 3.4 live-ball turnovers a game, the most in the league, and only 3 forced against 9 giveaways. Over 23 results his teams win 5.4 points of win chance more than expected (13-10). Three filmed games is still an early read.

viraj.headline: Gets beaten half the time, and wins the possession when he doesn't.
text: Viraj has been beaten on 8 of 16 shots, the highest rate in the league. When he stays in front, opponents shoot 25%, and Zach went 0 for 7 against him.
On offense he has 8 shots in 3 games at 25% TS, and his set-ups go to low-value spots (0.32 points a shot).
He is 0-3 on film with -28 on Win chance added, but 6-6 over every result, and his win impact is too close to call. Three filmed games is still an early read.
